summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a patient with refractory multiple myeloma, MDS with pancytopenia, and COPD, was admitted for acute on chronic renal failure and hypotension. His creatinine rose from 1.6 to 2.6, likely due to volume depletion, and improved with IV fluids. A new left lower lobe pneumonia was identified on chest X-ray and confirmed by CT, prompting treatment with IV cefepime, later transitioned to oral cefpodoxime. Urinalysis showed pyuria, and though culture results were inconclusive, treatment covered possible urinary infection. His multiple myeloma was managed with dexamethasone due to prior chemotherapy side effects. He remained stable, with resolution of renal dysfunction and no signs of heart failure. He was discharged home on oral antibiotics, allopurinol, and adjusted medications with follow-up plans.
